blocking_findings.text: The candidate claims the library is 'dependency-free' and 'has no required third-party package dependencies'.

blocking_findings.measured: The quoted sentence is the last sentence of content unit 0, section 'opening', slot 'opening' - an LLM-owned unit that cites dependency:none among its fact IDs. It is not in the identity section at all. The reviewer's section_id names 'identity', which is in _DETERMINISTIC_SECTIONS, so repair recorded unrepairable with the reason 'section identity is deterministic; its blocks change only when facts change' and never re-asked the unit that actually holds the sentence.
blocking_findings.note: prompts/independent_review.yaml line 126 names this exact phrase: 'an unscoped absolute dependency claim ("no dependencies", "dependency-free") that no dependency fact proves is REJECT_FACTUAL'. The authoring side wrote the phrase the review side is instructed to reject on sight; and the condition the rule attaches ('that no dependency fact proves') is not met here, because dependency:none is SUPPORTED with the evidence detail 'every `<dependency>` the POM declares is `test`, `provided` or optional'.

new_blocker.why_none_was_refuted: Re-ran origin/main's own scope_defect, absence_defect and factuality_defect against all three findings with this transaction's facts, README and original README: every one returns None. F01 and F03 escape because presentation_defect - the rule that a deterministic section's content is no stage's to revise - returns None immediately when criterion != 'presentation' (review.py line 333), and renderer_sentences is scoped to sentences the renderer writes inside sections an LLM otherwise owns, so rendered_defect does not see a fully deterministic section either. F07 escapes because factuality_defect returns None when fact_ids is empty ('no fact supports this claim' cites nothing, by definition) and absence_defect reads only the 'absent' array, which is empty.
new_blocker.the_machinery_did_work_on_the_rest: 5 of the reviewer's 8 findings were caught as the reviewer's own defect and recorded advisory: F02 (the quote contains the literal value of SUPPORTED fact package:version), F04 and F08 (rendered_defect - the quoted sentence is the renderer's own), F05 and F06 (absence_defect - the finding claims the candidate does not contain 'AlignmentValue' / 'DiagnosticSeverity', which the candidate contains). The same reviewer, in the same reply, filled 'absent' for F05 and F06 and left it empty for F03 and F07, which the candidate's bytes refute just as squarely. The check is exact when the reviewer fills the field the prompt requires and blind when it does not.
